title: Holmes at Home
format: solo narration in true crime form: cold open, the arrival, the timeline, the suspects, the reveal, the epilogue. 18 to 24 minutes, no ads read in character. the pipeline name is the brand; the voice is hers

fiction.disclosure: The case was invented on purpose, for people who like this format, and the show says so in one fast breath at the end: made up, nobody was hurt, no real case is being reopened. Also in the show notes and the episode description, because a listener who stops early should still have been told.

guardrails: no real case, real victim, real suspect or living person, at any point, including as a passing comparison
no invented case may borrow enough detail from a real one to be identifiable
the title, thumbnail and description never imply a real case: the fiction tag lives there too, because the end tag only reaches people who finish
police and forensic procedure stays generic and is never presented as a real account of a real force
canon only: the 1887 to 1927 stories are public domain, the modern adaptations are not, and none of their inventions are borrowed
cases resolve from letters, photographs and recordings, never by the narrator going somewhere and confronting somebody, because a solo-narrated pipeline has one voice and no cast

episode_zero.title: The Locked Sunroom
beats: cold open: a letter arrives postmarked from a village that is not on the map, and the narrator says the line about the case being invented
the arrival: what the envelope contained, described as evidence rather than exposition
the timeline: a dinner party, a conservatory, a window that was painted shut in 1974
the suspects: five guests, each with one detail that does not fit the room
the reveal: the detail was the paint, and the paint was the alibi
the epilogue: what the letter writer was actually asking for, which was never the case

why_invented: true crime as a genre runs on other people's worst days, and the format itself is the thing worth keeping: the timeline, the suspects, the reveal. invented cases keep every part of that and take nobody's grief as raw material.

narrator.who: the persona, speaking as herself: there is no detective character, no Holmes, no Watson, and nobody in the fiction is named
narrator.note: Holmes at Home is the name of the production pipeline, in the way a studio names a slate. the show is what the pipeline makes.
